chapter: Technique and the Covington band's sound
title: Whether Buddy Petit composed or read music
summary: Petit wrote no tunes but could read a little and taught the band new numbers by ear; few in the band read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah. That was pretty. Yeah, that was good. I was going to ask you about this band. If you had any pieces that you all composed, or did Buddy ever write any music? Do you know of any songs?

No, Buddy never did worry about no music like that. But he could spell a little bit. Buddy could read a little bit. Yeah, but he never did worry about. Or make up any tunes. I mean even if they weren't written
down, you know if he ever wrote any, or composed any, made them up or anything.

No. No. No. Sometime you take like, he get a number, and if he learned a number, he's going to come tell us, well we've got a new number. We just try it before people come in. We're going to play right there. All right after the banjo, get on in there and him and this boy, and that. Well them three they're going to slow, you know what I mean? Well a little while after that I come on in there and I'm hitting, you know what I mean? After I be hitting like that, well that tramo was going to come in there. So Edmund Hardy said well let's go, so we're going to play this thing a new number, you know what I mean? Well he done learned the number. Well that's really because I couldn't read at that time myself. But George he could read a little bit, and I think Edmund could read, but this man he couldn't read. No, and the drummer couldn't read, you know what I mean? And Buddy could read a little. Yeah, Buddy could read a little, he could spell.
